messages:
oliver: Heads up  hiring seasonal lead who starts 11/15, 6-month probation, team worried about year-end carryover and blackout during Dec 20Jan 2. Do probation rules block carryover?
nina: Probation doesn't automatically block carryover. Carryover eligibility is tied to being active on 12/31. The wrinkle is our policy of pausing certain benefits until probation ends for some hires  is that what you mean?
oliver: Yes, manager heard that benefits don't fully apply until after probation. They want to know if we need an exception so the seasonal lead can carry unused days into next year if still employed on 12/31 but probation ends after 1/15.
sophia: Policy snippet: 
hr-bot: ```
Carryover: Employees active on payroll on Dec 31 are eligible to carry unused PTO up to the cap. Benefit eligibility during probation: standard benefits apply unless specifically withheld in offer. Exceptions to benefits or carryover must be documented in the offer and approved by People Ops.
```
oliver: Ok, so offer language controls it. Manager didn't include any probation-exclusion language. That means standard carryover applies if they're on payroll 12/31?
nina: Correct. If no withholding language in offer, payroll treats them as eligible for carryover. If you want to withhold, that needs to be explicitly written and approved at offer time.
payroll-bot: FYI: payroll will apply carryover automatically for employees flagged as active on 12/31. To block carryover, People Ops must send a carryover-exclusion tag to payroll before Jan 7.
oliver: Two related asks: 1) during the blackout (12/201/2) the manager wants to require the seasonal lead to be on-call for one day. Can we mandate that without affecting carryover? 2) They want to offer a one-time onboarding sick-top-up (3 days) because role is customer-facing. How to route?
sophia: 1) Blackout scheduling rules allow managers to assign coverage; that doesn't change accrual or carryover. Make sure it's in the offer or onboarding notes. 2) Sick-top-up: manager submits People Ops request with business justification. We can approve one-time grants for customer-facing hires; if you want to auto-grant, include a clause in the offer and we'll tag payroll.
nina: Suggest adding two checklist items to the hire workflow: "Blackout coverage required? (Y/N)" and "Onboarding sick-top-up approved? (Y/N)" with manager justification attached. That keeps things consistent.
oliver: Perfect. I'll update the offer to state: "You may be scheduled for limited coverage during company holiday operations; standard PTO carryover applies if you remain an active employee on Dec 31." For the sick-top-up I'll ask manager to file the People Ops request and mark the checklist.
sophia: If People Ops approves the 3-day top-up, payroll needs the tag by Jan 7 to apply the one-time credit in the first pay period of the new year.
payroll-bot: Reminder: manual adjustments after payroll run require a ticket and can take 2 pay cycles.
oliver: Great, thanks. I'll circulate the updated offer language and the checklist changes. Closing the loop. :white_check_mark:
